overview: White defends e4 with the queen instead of a knight or e5, so Nf3 is blocked and the queen is early. Black can play 3...dxe4 4.Nxe4 Nf6 or ...Bf5, or 3...Nf6, and develops comfortably, usually reaching a normal Caro-Kann with the queen misplaced on f3. White hopes for tricks on the f-file and quick Bc4 or Bd3 development.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the e-pawn defended and develop with Bc4 or Bd3, Nge2 and castling.
Use the queen on f3 to pressure f7 and the long diagonal.

black_ideas.idea: Trade pawns with ...dxe4 and develop with ...Nf6 or ...Bf5, gaining tempi on the queen.
Keep the Caro-Kann structure and play ...e6 and ...Nd7.

typical_structures.structure: Caro-Kann set-up with ...c6 and an open d-file after the exchange on e4.

character.notes: Black has few risks and a comfortable game; the early queen rarely creates real threats.

soundness.notes: Playable but slightly awkward for White; not refuted.

structure.notes: Typical Caro-Kann with a half-open d-file after ...dxe4.

approach.notes: A sideline strong players seldom pick for White; mainly a change of pace.

level.notes: Few theoretical demands, but not a first-repertoire choice for White.

character.reason: Black gets an easy Caro-Kann with few risks.

structure.reason: Caro-Kann with a half-open d-file after ...dxe4.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom play the early queen against the Caro-Kann.

level.reason: Simple ideas but an unusual choice for White.

plans.reason: White's queen comes out early on f3.
